item.title: A Foreigner's Journey to Boston — Fri Nov 20, 7:30 PM — Buskirk-Chumley Theater
item.description:
Experience the magic of three legendary bands—Foreigner, Journey, and Boston—brought to life by a powerhouse tribute group. Fronted by Brandon Miller, touring guitarist of the Artimus Pyle Band and Rock and Roll Hall of Fame drummer of Lynyrd Skynyrd, A Foreigner’s Journey to Boston delivers the iconic hits that defined a generation.
With a setlist spanning the greatest hits of Foreigner, Journey, and Boston, this band brings the energy, passion, and nostalgia of classic rock to every performance.
“Don’t Stop Believing” — “More Than a Feeling” — “I Wanna Know What Love Is” — AND SO MUCH MORE!
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar, WFIU Community Calendar

item.title: Brown County Art Guild 2026 Annual Raffle — Sat Nov 21, 12:00 AM — Brown County Art Guild
item.description: Take a chance to win ‘Painters Point’, a beautiful original oil painting generously donated by Guild Artist, Allen Hutton. He strives to render the fleeting patterns of light and shadow with the simple purpose of preserving the reality of a landscape at a particular moment in time and season. Allen has achieved numerous awards and his art can be found in both private and corporate collections across the county. Tickets: 1 for $30, 2 for $50, or 5 for $100 Your generosity helps the Guild to preserve its historic collection, promote its award-winning artist members, and offer workshops and programs throughout the year! The drawing of the winning raffle ticket will be held at 3pm on Saturday, November 21, 2026, at the Guild. The winner need not be present for the drawing. Purchase options: In person at the Guild, call 812-988-6185 or purchase raffle tickets at: https://browncountyartguild.org/product/brown-county-art-guild-annual-raffle/ ——————————————————————————————————

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Sat Nov 21 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Sat Nov 21 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Sat Nov 21 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.description:
November 21 , 2026 BBBSCI hosts record-breaking annual gala, “The Main Event,” with Title Sponsor, Delta Faucet Company Get creative with other matches every other Saturday at the Indy Art Center!
Email Us to Learn More
Learn more:
Art Reach is a recurring event *almost every other Saturday, where matches learn from an experienced art teacher and create a masterpiece to take home.
Attend one or attend all, but each Art Reach session focuses on a different art method and unique project, so no two visits are the same! All skill levels welcome.
This event is great at instilling confidence in Littles (and Bigs) as they learn something new and bring their imagination alive.

item.title: Planes, Trains and Automobiles (1987) — Sun Nov 22, 7:00 PM — Buskirk Chumley Theater
item.description:
Prepare for family, food, and fun this Thanksgiving! Steve Martin and John Candy star in this classic 1987 comedy road trip film written, produced, and directed by John Hughes. Easily excitable Neal Page \(Steve Martin\) is somewhat of a control freak. Trying to get home to Chicago to spend Thanksgiving with his wife \(Laila Robins\) and kids, his flight is rerouted to a distant city in Kansas because of a freak snowstorm, and his sanity begins to fray. Worse yet, he is forced to bunk up with talkative Del Griffith \(John Candy\), whom he finds extremely annoying. Together they must overcome the insanity of holiday travel to reach their intended destination. Rated: RLength: 1hr 33minFormat: DCP
Source: Limestone Post

item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Mon Nov 23, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Going to college offers a variety of new freedoms, excitements, and difficulties as students make the transition away from home. Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Embedded Accessible Educational Services (AES) — Fri Nov 27, 8:00 AM — LGBTQ+ CULTURE CENTER
item.description:
At the LGBTQ+ Culture Center, we want every student to have the resources they need to thrive. Disabilities come in all shapes and sizes, and many are not visible to others. Accessible Educational Services (AES) partners with students to provide accommodations, support services, and tools that help create equal access and opportunity at IU. Kade Padgett, M.A., an AES Access Coordinator, is available at the LGBTQ+ Culture Center every Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. during drop-in advising hours. Whether you're curious about accommodations, have questions about the process, or simply want to learn more about available resources, we invite you to stop by and chat with Kade about the support options that may be available to you. All Indiana University events, groups, activities, educational, cultural, and historical observances welcome all members of the Indiana University community.
Source: IU LGBTQ+ Culture Center

item.description:
At the LGBTQ+ Culture Center, we want every student to have the resources they need to thrive. Disabilities come in all shapes and sizes, and many are not visible to others. Accessible Educational Services (AES) partners with students to provide accommodations, support services, and tools that help create equal access and opportunity at IU. Kade Padgett, M.A., an AES Access Coordinator, is available at the LGBTQ+ Culture Center every Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. during drop-in advising hours. Whether you're curious about accommodations, have questions about the process, or simply want to learn more about available resources, we invite you to stop by and chat with Kade about the support options that may be available to you. All Indiana University events, groups, activities, educational, cultural, and historical observances welcome all members of the Indiana University community.

item.title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour — Fri Dec 4, 1:00 PM — Lilly Library
item.description:
Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library — Fri Dec 4, 2:00 PM — Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.)
item.description:
You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) and The Signers (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/the-signers). Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.

item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Sat Dec 5 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Sat Dec 5 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery.
